ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all founders, officers, beneficiaries, and any related parties against the consolidated UN Security Council sanctions lists, OFAC SDN List, UK HM Treasury sanctions, EU restrictive measures, and the domestic lists maintained by the Panamanian UAF. Enhanced due diligence is required for any politically exposed person (PEP), including domestic PEPs, and for any operation originating in a jurisdiction identified as high-risk by FATF or the UAF. Continuous risk-based monitoring applies throughout the lifetime of the foundation; any positive hit must be escalated to the compliance officer of the registered agent and the UAF as applicable.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá – Portal de Servicios en Línea (https://www.registropublico.gob.pa)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names may be expressed in Spanish, English, or any language using the Latin alphabet. If the name uses a non-Latin script, a phonetic transliteration into Latin characters is mandatory for registry entry. For Private Interest Foundations, the name must contain the word 'Fundación' or its English equivalent 'Foundation' in accordance with Ley 25 de 12 de junio de 2013, and must be capable of being clearly pronounced and recorded in the Public Registry.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registro Público rejects a proposed foundation name, the applicant or its resident agent may file a motion for reconsideration (recurso de reconsideración) before the Director General of the Registro Público within three (3) working days of the notification of rejection. If reconsideration is denied or only partially granted, a contentious-administrative appeal (demanda contencioso-administrativa) may be filed within two months before the Sala Tercera de la Corte Suprema de Justicia. Alternatively, the applicant may immediately submit an alternative name reservation after the expiry of the original lawfully reserved name certificate if the grounds of rejection are of a formal nature.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office usage is permissible for administrative and mail-forwarding purposes for an offshore Private Interest Foundation with no physical Panamanian business operations. However, the statutory registered agent must maintain a physical working office in Panama; the foundation itself is not required to have a physical commercial establishment in Panama if all substantive manufacturing, sales, and operational activities take place abroad.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (≈5%). There is a very low statistical probability of unannounced on-site inspection of the foundation's foreign manufacturing premises because such operations are outside Panamanian territorial jurisdiction. The Panamanian Registered Agent may be subject to occasional compliance inspections by the UAF or notarial/registry oversight, but these are administrative reviews conducted at the agent's office, not at the extraterritorial business location.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (General Law on Private Interest Foundations), as amended; Articles 18-25 for public deed and registration; Executive Decree No. 6 of 1996,
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Fundación de Interés Privado (Public Deed of Private Interest Foundation)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital. The founder must endow the foundation with assets or capital sufficient for its stated purpose (commonly USD 100 or equivalent); no escrow or deposit account is required by law. The initial endowment is declared in the foundation charter and certified by the notary.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: that the initial endowment of the Foundation, contributed by the Founder, is accepted and recorded for the development of Cosplay Prop Apparel Manufacture. RESOLVED: that the registered office located at Panama City, Republic of Panama, is adopted as the Foundation’s legal domicile. RESOLVED: that the Founder appoints the Foundation Council consisting of three members, and that [Name 1], [Name 2], and [Name 3] are hereby elected as members. RESOLVED: that [Name 1] serves as President, [Name 2] as Secretary, and [Name 3] as Treasurer. RESOLVED: that the President and Secretary are jointly and severally authorized to execute all filings and sign agreements with the Public Registry, tax authorities, and any licensing body.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Notarize the Foundation Public Deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notario Público de Panamá (Panamanian Public Notary)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a licensed Panamanian attorney to draft the Escritura Pública. Appear before the notary with the Founder or authorized representative, present identity documents, and sign the deed. The notary embeds the deed in a protocol and issues certified copies.
required_dossiers: Passport or national identity card of the Founder
Draft foundation charter (estatutos)
Certificate of notarial representation, if applicable
Preliminary risk assessment for low-risk commercial activity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary rejects the deed for omissions, correct the charter text and resubmit within 3 business days; no additional registry penalty if completed administratively.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit Public Deed to Public Registry for Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarial copy (or certified copy) at the Public Registry. Pay the official registration fees and wait for the assigned entry number. Provide any additional clarifications requested by the registrar within the curing period.
required_dossiers: Original and two certified copies of the Public Deed
Payment receipt for state registration fees
Cover letter requesting inscription
Completed PIF registration form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a caution notice (reparo) is issued, address the objection within 30 days. Re-submit the deed with amendments or supportive documents; additional registry fees may apply only if the objection is not cleared.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Taxpayer Identification Number (RUC) from Tax Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI del Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the RUC application online or in person using the registered Foundation Deed. Designate the legal representative and state the economic activity code ISIC 3240. Obtain the taxpayer certification and upload required corporate documents.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of registered Foundation Public Deed
Certified copy of Foundation Council appointment
Proof of registered address in Panama
Passport copies of legal representative and tax agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RUC application is rejected for incomplete information, reconstitute the file with the DGI's e-government portal and provide the missing notarial certificate within 5 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register as Employer with Social Security Fund
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Caja de Seguro Social (CSS) — Servicio de Inscripción de Empresas
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the PIF as an employer if it will have employees. Submit the RUC and foundation resolution to the CSS employer registry. Obtain the CSS employer number for payroll reporting and worker contributions.
required_dossiers: RUC certificate
Registered foundation charter
Employer registration form (F-1)
Copy of board resolution appointing the persons responsible for payroll
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CSS rejects the file, correct the legal representative identification or company category and re-submit within 10 business days; no penalty if the error is corrected before payroll begins.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Municipal Business Operation Notice (Aviso de Operación)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alcaldía del Municipio de Panamá — Oficina de Avisos de Operación
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Aviso de Operación declaration for the business address. Provide the RUC, foundation deed, lease contract, and municipal zoning compliance. Pay the municipal fee based on assessed lease and economic activity.
required_dossiers: RUC certificate
Lease or title deed for the registered office/factory
Certified copy of foundation registration and council appointment
Industrial zoning statement from the Municipality
Fire safety inspection report (preliminary)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Municipality denies the Aviso for zoning non-compliance, apply for a special use permit or relocate the manufacturing premises to an industrial-zoned area; file an amended Aviso within 15 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Industrial Registry with Ministry of Commerce and Industries
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) — Dirección General de Industrias
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the manufacturing unit under the Industrial Registry. Present the Municipal Aviso, environmental registration (where applicable), and equipment inventory. Obtain the Certificado de Registro Industrial enabling lawful industrial production and import duty benefits.
required_dossiers: Aviso de Operación
RUC certificate
Notarized foundation charter
Environmental registration (Category I) from MiAMBIENTE
List of machinery and description of manufacturing operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the industrial registry application is suspended, supplement the file with corrected machinery values or production statements and re-submit within 30 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) — Dirección General de Industrias

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) — Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category I — Environmental Registration (No full EIA required). Activities limited to apparel assembly, sewing, and wig fabrication from non-toxic synthetic fibers.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Industrial wastewater must comply with Resolución AG-0458-2018 from MINSA (BOD≤150 mg/L, TSS≤150 mg/L, pH 6-9). No hazardous VOC emissions expected; ventilation must keep workspace air contaminants below OSHA-equivalent limits. Textile waste and synthetic wig trimmings must be handled as non-hazardous solid waste and removed by licensed haulers.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certification from Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá: requires smoke detectors, extinguishers, and unobstructed exits. Structural load inspection certificate issued by the Municipality or a qualified engineer for the fabrication floor. Occupational safety clearance from Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL) for machine guards and ergonomic workstations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF), Republic of Panama; online fiscal portal: 'T@-PÁ' (https://tapa.mef.gob.pa). Customs enforcement: Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA); legal-entity registry: Registro Público de Panamá.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) as the sole prudential banking and financial services regulator; Panama has no central bank of issue. The US dollar circulates as full legal tender, and the Panamanian balboa exists only as coins pegged 1:1 to the USD. Monetary policy is de facto determined by the US Federal Reserve. The Banco Nacional de Panamá acts as a state-owned fiscal agent but does not exercise central banking powers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama maintains complete and unrestricted currency convertibility. There are no exchange control laws, no capital controls, and no restrictions on current or capital account transactions. The absence of a domestic issuance currency eliminates convertibility friction. Profit remittances, intercompany dividends, and capital contributions may be freely transferred in USD, provided that underlying banking and AML/KYC procedures are satisfied. The territorial tax system applies to operations with Panamanian-source revenue; for a Private Interest Foundation (PIF) undertaking foreign e-commerce sales, the exemption from Panamanian tax on foreign-source income is available but requires documentary proof that profits derived from the international sale of costumes and wigs are not sourced in Panama.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Panama imposes no statutory export proceeds surrender requirement and no mandatory conversion ratio. Exporters and private interest foundations may retain full proceeds in USD or any other currency. There is no deadline for repatriation, no compulsory sale to a designated bank, and no obligation to convert export receipts into local legal tender. The only compliance duties relate to anti-money laundering rules: transaction records, due diligence on counterparties, and reporting of suspicious cross-border movements to the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) under SBP Rule 4-2019.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability as a primary treasury or clearing bank; Medium viability as a merchant-payment processor. Under Panamanian banking law (Decree-Law 9 of 1998 and SBP Rule 4-2019), only SBP-licensed banks and financial entities may lawfully receive deposits or provide clearing and settlement services to persons residing in Panama. Foreign electronic money institutions (EMIs) such as Wise, Airwallex, Mercury, and Payoneer do not possess SBP licenses for deposit-taking or local settlement. Using such EMIs for a Panamanian PIF's main operating account carries elevated legal and de-risking risk, including account freezes, compliance suspensions, and regulatory censure. However, online payment aggregators such as Stripe and Shopify Payments may be used as non-deposit, payment processing gateways for customer credit card transactions, provided that final treasury balances are periodically swept into an SBP-supervised commercial bank account. The PIF should ensure the processor's merchant agreement permits the underlying business model and supports cross-border settlement into a Panamanian bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical attendance is generally mandatory for a Private Interest Foundation because the service provider must obtain the 'economic rationale' and 'source of wealth' information from the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO). Most tier-1 Panamanian banks require the founding beneficiary and at least one director to appear at an in-person client interview at the bank's main office in Panama City; a notarized and apostilled power of attorney appointing a licensed Panamanian attorney or trustee permits remote facilitation, but the initial interview must still be conducted on-site with the attorney and an identified representative of the foundation. Some banks now allow a hybrid remote opening using a certified video call, original documents delivered through a reputable courier, and a sworn signature verification at the Embassy; nevertheless, as a conservative compliance blueprint, the PIF should budget for at least one physical director visit. Final form signing by all directors or the appointed special agent is normally notarized before a Panamanian notary public.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Private Interest Foundation confidentiality: beneficiaries are set out in the private founding clause and not visible in the public registry.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A certified copy of the Foundation Deed, the notarized private clause, an appointed Protector certificate, a sworn UBO declaration to the bank compliance department, and a copy of the initial capital payment receipt with the amount of the paid-in endowment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital transfers from multiple foreign founders (non-resident natural persons) used for the initial foundation capital.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sworn source-of-funds and source-of-wealth statements for every contributing founder, independent bank reference letters from each remitting institution, the capital contribution resolution, and audited net-worth statements where equivalent to the contribution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: E-commerce cosplay apparel business generates high-volume cross-border card payments and card-not-present transactions from diverse jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The underlying online store contract with Stripe/Shopify, a copy of the product catalogue and pricing, supplier invoices for synthetic wigs and fabrics, logistics and export custom declarations, monthly merchant activity reports, and an independent AML transaction monitoring report showing negative sanctions screening against the consolidated UN, EU, and OFAC lists.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Hybrid legal status and territorial tax exemption create an appearance of tax-driven structuring or shell-entity risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A licensed Panamanian tax counsel opinion confirming that foreign-source e-commerce revenues fall outside Panama's territorial tax jurisdiction, a transfer-pricing memo for inbound materials used in costume production, CRS/FATCA filings demonstrating transparent disclosure, and a functional operational substance report listing the foundation's employees, storage, and real economic activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Registered agent address is the only physical presence of the foundation, a common shell-like red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A letter from the licensed resident agent confirming administrative substance, a full notarized office lease or shared-space service contract, an outsourced accounting and bookkeeping engagement, and evidence of production or manufacturing relationships (e.g., cut-and-sew contracts, quality-control inspections) to prove operational activity beyond passive invoicing.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The recommended compliant routing for capital contributions is a SWIFT MT103 in USD from the founder's bank to the PIF's USD-denominated account at an SBP-licensed bank. The MT103 must identify the beneficiary as the exact Private Interest Foundation name, the beneficiary account number, the foundation's registered agent, and the remittance information field (field 70) must state 'Foundation Capital Contribution – [Foundation Name]'. Because Panama has no exchange control restrictions, no panamanian central bank prior authorization is required; however, the receiving bank must screen the transaction for OFAC/UN/EU sanctions and verify the originator's details. The bank's AML unit may request a Board Resolution confirming the contribution, a notarized foundation certificate of good standing issued within one month, and a sworn UBO declaration before crediting the funds. For transfers originating from a jurisdiction that is a non-cooperative tax jurisdiction or grey-listed, the bank will likely request enhanced due diligence including source-of-funds bank reference and legal certificate from the paying bank. Correspondent routing is through major US clearing institutions (JP Morgan, Bank of America) or directly via Cascadia/Credit Suisse networks, with typical USD clearing settlement within one to two business days.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For trade disbursements to foreign suppliers of synthetic fabrics, thread, cosmetics-grade polypropylene for wigs, and packaging materials, the primary clearing rails are SWIFT MT103 direct transfers and documentary commercial letters of credit (MT700). A sight documentary credit is appropriate where the supplier requires signed commercial invoice, bill of lading or airway bill, insurance certificate, and a third-party inspection certificate. For regular raw material purchases below USD 100,000 per lot, direct MT103 wires are faster and cheaper; but the bank's trade finance desk should be consulted because Panama is a full US-dollar clearing corridor and there is no domestic cross-border bulk ACH system. All outgoing transfer instructions must include the beneficiary's IBAN, CLABE (Mexico) or SWIFT/BIC, the expected cost-center and purchase-order reference, and explicit statement in field 70 such as 'INV[invoice number] – [PIF name] – Ref: Cosplay Supplies'. Where Chinese suppliers are paid in CNY, disbursements may be executed through an offshore CNY clearing arrangement or by converting USD in the Hong Kong offshore renminbi (CNH) market; the bank will require the underlying purchase contract to support the currency conversion and to manage anti-money laundering exposure. The PIF should maintain a consolidated payment matrix and use SWIFT GPI tracking for end-to-end transparency and settlement acceleration.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain vanilla deliverable foreign exchange forward (FX forward) on USD/EUR and USD/CNH, with a tenor up to 12 months and underlying trade payables/receivables documentation.
Non-deliverable forward (NDF) on onshore CNY (USD/CNY) executed offshore through an international bank, used in connection with Chinese supplier invoices that require USD settling on a non-CNH basis.

Cross-currency swap (CCS) between USD and EUR or USD and CNH for notional hedging of long-term recurring trade obligations; the swap must be documented by an ISDA Master Agreement under English law and supported by the foundation's annual procurement forecasts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Private Interest Foundation Government Fee (Tasa Anual de Fundación)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) – Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF); remitted by the resident agent through Banco Nacional de Panamá
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within the first 10 days of January (Ley 25 de 1995, Article 34); the first-year fee is collected at registration and subsequent fees fall due in January
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment incurs a US$50 statutory surcharge; sustained non-payment for more than 12 months impairs issuance of good standing certificates, blocks Public Registry transactions, and may trigger administrative strike-off/cancellation of the foundation at the request of the DGI.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is required for a passive Private Interest Foundation. A certified independent audit becomes mandatory only where the foundation derives Panamanian-source commercial revenue exceeding US$1,000,000 or the DGI classifies it as a large taxpayer; foreign-source passive foundations remain audit-exempt.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Panama adopts IFRS as the formal accounting framework if financial statements are prepared; passive PIFs may maintain simplified internal cash-basis records because there is no statutory public filing of annual accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The resident agent must perform an annual AML/CFT due-diligence review under Ley 23 de 2015 and obtain written confirmation of current beneficial owners and foundation council members. Because a Private Interest Foundation has no share capital, share-transfer filings do not apply; any change in beneficiaries or council composition must be evidenced by a resolution or deed and mirrored in the foundation's private registers held by the resident agent.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Foundation registry of founder, council members and beneficiaries
Registered agent's beneficial ownership register (AML file)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $800 – $1,250 per year (resident-agent fee inclusive of government-fee handling)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $2,500 – $5,000 (voluntary audit or triggered only by large-taxpayer status)
